query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Systematic variation of the percentage of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr elements in the HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy (HEA) will result in a change in the mechanical properties, specifically yield strength and hardness, due to the alteration of the lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening mechanisms.
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of elemental composition by changing the percentage of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr elements
generation.conditions: Room temperature, various mechanical testing conditions (e.g., tensile testing, compression testing, hardness testing)
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: Cause-and-effect relationship between elemental composition and mechanical properties, where changes in elemental composition alter the lattice distortion and solid solution strengthening, leading to changes in yield strength and hardness
generation.predicted_outcome: A 10% increase in Hf content will result in a 15% increase in yield strength (from 1000 MPa to 1150 MPa) and a 10% increase in hardness (from 500 HV to 550 HV), relative to the baseline composition (Hf40Nb20Ta20Ti10Zr10)
generation.boundary: Elemental composition range: Hf (30-50 at%), Nb (15-30 at%), Ta (15-30 at%), Ti (5-20 at%), Zr (5-20 at%)
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between elemental composition and mechanical properties is still unknown, and the effects of other microstructural features, such as grain size and precipitates, may influence the results

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled variable experiment with systematic variation of elemental composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength and hardness do not change by more than 5% (i.e., < 50 MPa and < 25 HV, respectively) in response to a 10% change in Hf content, then the hypothesis is falsified

frame.goal: understanding the effects of changing elemental composition on mechanical properties
frame.limitation: individual constituents' effects on mechanical properties are unknown
root_cause_cues: individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored

precedents.outcome: The AT-SPS-HPT specimen achieved the lowest oxygen content and was the only sample with a single-phase bcc random solid solution and zero porosity

precedents.problem: Investigating the tensile and creep properties of Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 high entropy alloy and the effect of gravity casting versus suction-assisted casting followed by Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP)
precedents.outcome: The HIP process induced the formation of a secondary Hexagonal Close Packed (HCP) phase in addition to the initial Body Centered Cubic (BCC) phase

precedents.outcome: The alloy achieved an ultrahigh ultimate tensile strength of 2.15 GPa with a tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature
